claims.access_scope: Reaction entry, exact structures and cited publication abstracts; not full primary assay-data audit
claims.claim: The exact reaction converts CHEBI:15413 to CHEBI:17846, (2S)-naringenin, with EC 5.5.1.6. Rhea also notes spontaneous cyclization. This does not establish the physiological rate or stereoselectivity of uncatalyzed conversion in Cannabis.

The alfalfa reference has experimental-evidence-coded function text for tetrahydroxychalcone cyclization and a substrate-specific Km annotation. The generic catalytic-activity record lacks a Rhea cross-reference. This is reference-organism annotation evidence, not a Cannabis assay.
claims.next_step: Audit the primary assays and map the reference catalytic-site features before making an exact-substrate candidate-model addition.

claims.claim: The reviewed hop CHIL1 entry carries EC 5.5.1.6 by similarity but describes stabilization of the ring-opened chalconoid by binding. The EC label cannot be treated as experimental cyclization evidence.

This Cannabis lead has an automated ARBA function annotation naming the substrate and naringenin product. The full-proteome screen matches it to P28012 at 53.8 percent identity, 52.6 percent query coverage and 82.0 percent reference coverage. Automated annotation and homology do not establish experimental activity; the WGS sequence caution is retained.

next_test: Review all reference assay and noncatalytic evidence separately, inspect sequence/domain architecture and aligned catalytic residues, then assay prioritized Cannabis proteins against authentic tetrahydroxychalcone. Quantify both naringenin enantiomers with chiral separation and time-matched no-enzyme controls to distinguish stereoselective catalysis from spontaneous cyclization. Do not assume reverse catalysis or complete precursor supply.
